question: How did a one-string bowed instrument with no frets come to be called the marine trumpet?
answer: By playing only a trumpet's notes. The tromba marina's player touches its long string lightly at its still points, drawing out harmonics, the same series a valveless trumpet plays. A shoe-shaped bridge with one loose leg drums against the soundboard, adding a brassy rattle. Why marina, nobody knows; German convents called it the nuns' fiddle.
move: Two instruments that share a limit can end up sharing a voice.
reference: Adkins & Dickinson, A Trumpet by Any Other Name: A History of the Trumpet Marine, Frits Knuf, 1991
